Obstructions and counterexamples · paper

Counterexample: unit transport delay does not imply pointwise sublinearity

A proved abstract counterexample has delay-one matching, linear crossing stock and linearly large alternating row imbalance. It refutes the general inference to pointwise sublinearity; it is not a canonical Chomp counterexample.

Paper proof with recorded review

This is a mathematical paper proof with the evidence recorded below. Its status does not by itself imply a checked Lean formalization.

Scientific review

Review verdict: accepted. Evidence and exact scope are linked above.

Statement

There exists an abstract signed event stream with a capacity-one opposite-sign matching of delay exactly1 and signed crossing inventory O(n), but pointwise imbalance not o(n).

Hypotheses and scope

  • Abstract dated token stream only, not a canonical Chomp realization.

Proof text

1. For each k>=1 put2k positive tokens at2k and2k negative tokens at2k+1, pairing equal local indices. Every token has one distinct partner one row away.

2. Every completed two-row pair contributes zero to the signed prefix. At cut2k the prefix and crossing stock are2k; at cut2k+1 they are0. Hence stock<=n, also o(n^2).

3. Pointwise imbalance is2k at2k and-2k at2k+1, so its absolute value divided by n tends to 1 on both subsequences. This refutes exactly the claimed inference, without asserting any canonical counterexample.

Formalization correspondence

This statement was independently audited on paper. The audit did not produce a new Lean formalization of the derived statement; its listed formal dependencies have separate verification receipts.

Verification evidence

The displayed statement, explicit hypotheses and full linked derivations received renewed model-assisted mathematical review. This is separate from Lean kernel verification. Fresh finite-certificate checks validate only their stated bases and finite obligations; all-index conclusions also require the written induction.
